verses.1: Having narrated this, Rama of immeasurable splendor then again spoke these righteous words to Lakshmana in the presence of his brothers.
verses.2: He spoke about inviting Vasistha, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kashyapa, and all other chief Brahmins who are appointed for the Ashwamedha sacrifice.
verses.3: O Lakshmana, having assembled all these and consulted with them, I shall release a horse endowed with auspicious marks, with proper ritual observance.
verses.4: Having heard that statement spoken by Rama, Lakshmana, of swift valor, summoned all the Brahmins and presented them to Rama.
verses.5: Having seen Rama, who was god-like, very difficult to overcome, and had just bowed at their feet, they honored him with their blessings.
verses.6: Then, the highly renowned Rama, with folded hands, explained his intention regarding the Ashwamedha sacrifice to the foremost Brahmins.
verses.7: Having heard Rama's intention, all the Brahmins bowed down to Shiva and then honored the Ashwamedha sacrifice in every way.
verses.8: Then, having heard the words of wonderful insight from those chief Brahmins regarding the Ashwamedha, he (Rama) became greatly pleased.
verses.9: Having understood their decision, Rama then said to Lakshmana, "Send messengers quickly to the great-souled Sugriva."
verses.10: Come with many great forest-dwelling monkeys to indeed enjoy this great festival, and may you be well.
verses.11: Let Vibhishana, of unequalled valor, come to the great Ashwamedha sacrifice, surrounded by many Rakshasas who can travel at will.
verses.12: Let all the highly fortunate kings who wish me well come quickly with their followers to witness this unsurpassed sacrifice.
verses.13: Lakshmana, invite all those Brahmins who are devoted to dharma and have gone to other countries for the Ashwamedha sacrifice.
verses.14: O mighty-armed one, let all sages whose wealth is penance, all Brahmins who have gone to other countries along with their wives, and similarly musicians, actors, and dancers be invited.
verses.15: O mighty-armed one, let a very large sacrificial enclosure be arranged in the Naimisha forest near the Gomati river, for that indeed is an unsurpassed meritorious act.
verses.16: And O mighty-armed one, let peace rites be performed everywhere.
verses.17: O delight of the Raghus, let hundreds of knowers of dharma, having experienced this great and unsurpassed chief of sacrifices in Naimisha...
verses.18: O knower of dharma, let all those people be quickly invited, so that they will be satisfied, nourished, and properly honored, thereby attaining great joy.
verses.19: O mighty one, let a hundred thousand cartloads of excellent rice grains and ten thousand cartloads of sesame and mung beans be sent ahead.
verses.20: Therefore, suitable oil and collected spices, along with chickpeas, horse gram, black gram, and salt, should also be taken.
verses.21: Bharata should go forth at the head, having placed many crores of gold and hundreds more of other gold wealth, with careful arrangement.
verses.22: Along the way, there should be market streets, and all actors and dancers, as well as many cooks and perpetually youthful women.
verses.23: Indeed, let the armies go forth with Bharata, and also the merchants, the strong and old, and the well-prepared Brahmins.
verses.24: Also, workers, carpenters, treasurers, merchants, all my mothers, and the inner chambers of the princes should similarly accompany them.
verses.25: Rama commanded that the greatly renowned Bharata should proceed first, carrying his golden idol of Sita, who represented his wife for the initiation, and also leading those who were knowledgeable in the rituals.
verses.26: The mighty Rama, the best among men, commanded that splendid temporary dwellings be arranged for the powerful kings and their retinues. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 91 ।। Thus ends the ninety-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
